newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: ODS'S PILIP PLAYS DOWN CHANCE OF EARLY CZECH POLLS.
newsitem.headline: ODS'S PILIP PLAYS DOWN CHANCE OF EARLY CZECH POLLS.

text.p: A senior member of the ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS) indicated on Thursday his party would not aim for early lower house elections if it won or lost Senate polls next week, CTK news agency reported.
Local analysts have speculated that the ODS-led coalition, which lost its lower house majority in June elections, could seek early polls if it won the Senate race.
CTK quoted ODS vice-chairman Ivan Pilip as telling a news conference that his party would use the increased stability if it won to speed up the pace of the country's reforms.

Pilip added that if the opposition Social Democrats, who emerged surprisingly strong from the June polls, won the Senate race, the government would still attempt to continue with its programme, but not at any cost, CTK said.

"We think that if the Social Democrats win strongly in the Senate, the destructive policy of parliament would strenghten rather and I am very concerned that concrete steps leading to a strenghtening of order in the Czech Republic would be extremely complicated," CTK quoted Pilip as saying.
"We would try to continue with them as much as possible, but of course only as far as we could follow our programme."

Czechs will cast ballots next week in the first round of Senate elections, which were seen as an unimportant race until the coalition led by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus unexpectedly lost its lower house majority in June, gaining 99 of the 200 seats.

A total of 81 senators will be elected under a first past the post system. It is expected that in most of them it will be a direct clash of ODS and the Social Democrats unlike in the lower house elections which are held under a proportional representation system.
